title: Shape and size errors: reading a traceback

questions.q: Where in a traceback do you find the error itself?
options: The first line of the frames
questions.why: Python prints the deepest call last, then the error. The engine's frames sit at the top.

questions.q: The size of tensor a (4) must match the size of tensor b (16) at non-singleton dimension 1, on latents. What does it mean?
options: Two model families met, with different channel counts
questions.answer: Two model families met, with different channel counts
questions.why: A latent's dimension 1 is its channels.

questions.q: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (77x2048 and 768x320), in a sampler. What do you check first?
options: That the text encoder fits the model
questions.answer: That the text encoder fits the model
questions.why: Width 2048 went into a layer built for 768. ComfyUI's own tip says to check CLIP loaders.

questions.q: You feed ImageBatch a 64 by 64 and a 128 by 128 image. What happens?
options: The second is resized to 64 by 64, with no message
The first is resized to 128 by 128
It keeps both as they are
questions.answer: The second is resized to 64 by 64, with no message
questions.why: We ran it: the result is (2, 64, 64, 3).

questions.q: Why does a batch of 1 hide a mismatch that a batch of 2 reveals?
options: A size of 1 broadcasts against anything
A batch of 1 skips the check
questions.answer: A size of 1 broadcasts against anything
questions.why: Torch stretches a size-1 axis. The lab gives (3, 4, 8, 8) with no error, and fails on 2 against 3.

questions.q: An error appears in KSampler. Is the sampler the likely cause?
options: Often not: it runs the model, so faults in the model, conditioning or latent surface there
questions.answer: Often not: it runs the model, so faults in the model, conditioning or latent surface there
questions.why: Read the frames below it and the sizes in the message.
